hints.junior: The bug isn't the effect's dependency array — it's that the filtered list existed as its own state at all, a second copy of something already knowable from items + search text.
hints.mid: A stored derived value plus an effect to sync it is a second source of truth waiting for one update path to forget to trigger it.
hints.staff: A useEffect whose only job is keeping one state variable in sync with another is a category error, not a missing dependency.

hints.junior: Read both versions side by side — the fixed one has no separate filteredItems state at all, so there's nothing left to go stale.
hints.mid: The fixed version's useMemo is there for performance only, not correctness — a plain inline expression would be just as correct, only slower.
hints.staff: No dependency array to get wrong, no effect to forget — the fixed version structurally cannot let filteredItems and items disagree.

hints.junior: If you can calculate a value from state you already have, calculate it every render instead of storing a second copy.
hints.mid: useMemo here only skips redoing the work when dependencies haven't changed — it still recomputes correctly whenever they have.
hints.staff: State should hold the smallest set of values that can't be derived from anything else — everything else is a view computed on demand.

hints.junior: Not everything computed should skip state — if a value needs to remember something its current inputs no longer contain, it's real state.
hints.mid: The test: does the value have meaning independent of its current inputs, or is it always just 'whatever recomputing right now would give'?
hints.staff: The same bug shows up in Redux: a reducer duplicating data another slice owns, synced by a second action creator, is this exact pattern at the store level.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about a filtered list that showed items you'd already deleted, because the filtered result was stored as its own state instead of just being computed.
The fix is simple: if you can calculate a value from state you already have, just calculate it every render instead of keeping a second copy around.
Compare the two code paths — one keeps a separate synced copy that can drift, the other computes the value fresh every time so there's nothing to keep in sync.
If it can be computed from state you already have, don't give it its own state. Compute it every render instead, and the sync bug becomes impossible.
